headline: Last days at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Last days at Sagamore Hill
summary: Roosevelt is at Sagamore Hill; nothing else is recorded.

headline: A Progressive send-off in New York
summary: New York Progressives throw Roosevelt a farewell dinner at a city roof garden. Albert Beveridge speaks, and Roosevelt follows with an attack on two party bosses, Republican William Barnes Jr. and Tammany's Charles Murphy.

events.detail: Farewell dinner from New York Progressives; Beveridge speaks

headline: Sailing for South America
summary: At 1 p.m. Roosevelt, in a gray suit and hat, sails from Brooklyn on the Vandyck with Edith, cousin Margaret Roosevelt, naturalist George Cherrie, Anthony Fiala and his secretary Frank Harper. Crowds pack the ship, pier and streets; the Progressives send a band, and envoys of three South American republics see him off.

events.detail: Sails from Pier 8, Brooklyn, on the Vandyck
Big send-off with a Progressive band and three South American ambassadors

uncertain: The record does not give Margaret Roosevelt's exact kinship to TR.

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Writing for Boys' Life at sea
summary: Aboard ship, Roosevelt writes an article for Boys' Life that will run in December.

headline: No answer on 1916
summary: From the ship, Roosevelt writes William Allen White that he will give no flat yes or no about the 1916 nomination.

events.detail: Declines to commit either way on 1916

letters.topic: Will not say yes or no about 1916

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Ashore in Barbados
summary: At Bridgetown, Barbados, Roosevelt gives a short speech, tours the town and lunches with the governor. Naturalist Leo Miller joins the expedition. In Brazil, Kermit turns 24.

events.detail: Sightseeing and lunch with the governor

headline: Eleanor's birthday at sea
summary: The party is at sea. Back home, his niece Eleanor Roosevelt turns 29.

headline: Word of Timothy Woodruff's death
summary: While Roosevelt is at sea, Timothy Woodruff dies in the United States. He had been Roosevelt's lieutenant governor and a Bull Moose backer in 1912.

events.detail: Death of his former lieutenant governor Timothy Woodruff

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Edith on a lifted burden
summary: At sea, Edith writes Bamie that her husband seems freed of the Progressive Party, like Christian in Pilgrim's Progress shedding his bundle.

events.detail: Edith writes Bamie about TR's relief

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Brazil's welcome at Bahia
summary: Officials greet Roosevelt at Bahia, where Governor Seabra and Mayor Brandao receive him. After breakfast he meets the city council at City Hall, gives a speech and tours the city. Kermit, building bridges for the Anglo-Brazilian Iron Company, joins the party.

events.detail: Officials greet him; Governor Seabra and Mayor Brandao host a reception
Meets the city council in City Hall

headline: Father and son on film
summary: Back at sea, Roosevelt and Kermit are caught on film aboard the Vandyck. It is the 15th birthday of his nephew Sheffield Cowles.

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Steaming south
summary: Roosevelt's party is at sea aboard the Vandyck, bound for South America.

headline: Crowds in Rio de Janeiro
summary: Officials greet Roosevelt in Rio, a great public reception fills the Naval Arsenal, and he calls on President Hermes da Fonseca and Foreign Minister Lauro Muller.

events.detail: Large reception in the Naval Arsenal
Calls on President da Fonseca and Lauro Muller

headline: Breakfast with Brazil's president
summary: Roosevelt breakfasts with President da Fonseca, tours the Supreme Court and Military College, speaks to the YMCA, and spends the evening at the Russian ballet.

events.detail: Visits the Supreme Court and Military College

headline: Science and an embassy reception
summary: Roosevelt tours Rio's Bacteriological Institute and is guest of honor at a reception hosted by the American ambassador, Edwin Morgan.

headline: "American Internationalism" in Rio
summary: The party goes up Tijuca Peak and attends the president's garden party in the Botanical Gardens. At the national university, Roosevelt lectures on "American Internationalism."

headline: Birdsong on the bay
summary: On a cruise around the bay, Roosevelt listens to the birds. He visits the Naval School and receives a group of teachers and advanced students. Edith writes a friend that she finds Brazil lovely.

events.detail: Bay excursion; listens to bird calls
Edith writes Miss Eustace in praise of Brazil

headline: Petropolis, then Sao Paulo
summary: The party visits the mountain town of Petropolis and then leaves for Sao Paulo.

headline: Turning 55 in Sao Paulo
summary: On his 55th birthday, Roosevelt is received by President Alves of Sao Paulo, sees the city and lectures at the university on "Character and Civilization."

headline: Touring Sao Paulo industry
summary: Roosevelt inspects local industry, including the Anglo-Brazilian Iron Company where Kermit works.

events.detail: Inspects factories and the Anglo-Brazilian Iron Company

headline: Heading south for Montevideo
summary: Roosevelt leaves Sao Paulo, bound for Montevideo.

headline: A cattle ranch in Parana
summary: In Parana, the travelers pause at Morungava to see a ranch run by Brazil Land, Cattle and Packing Company.

events.detail: Tours a ranch run by Brazil Land, Cattle and Packing Company

headline: Crossing Parana
summary: The party is in Parana. At home, another installment of Roosevelt's "Chapters of a Possible Autobiography" appears.

headline: Through Santa Catarina
summary: The party crosses the Brazilian state of Santa Catarina. In New York, The Outlook prints Roosevelt's "American Internationalism."

headline: Rolling across Rio Grande do Sul
summary: Crossing Rio Grande do Sul, the train pauses at Cruz Alta and again at Santa Maria.

events.detail: Train halts at Cruz Alta, then Santa Maria

headline: Greeted at the Uruguayan border
summary: Passing through Porto Alegre, Roosevelt is met at the frontier by officials from Uruguay.

events.detail: Uruguayan officials welcome him at the border

headline: Lunch with Uruguay's president
summary: In Montevideo, Roosevelt lunches with President Batlle y Ordonez and attends a state dinner before leaving for Buenos Aires. Back home it is election day. He writes Frank Chapman about the trip and a cougar skull from the West.

events.detail: Election day in the United States
Writes Chapman about the journey and a western cougar skull

letters.topic: News of the trip; a cougar skull found in the West

headline: Welcome to Buenos Aires
summary: U.S. Minister John Garrett and Argentine officials greet the party in Buenos Aires. The American community holds a reception, the Roosevelts are guests of President Saenz Pena, and Roosevelt calls on acting President de la Plaza.

events.detail: Welcomed by Minister Garrett and officials
Calls on acting President de la Plaza

headline: In Buenos Aires
summary: Roosevelt is in Buenos Aires; nothing else is recorded.

headline: "Democratic Ideals" at the Colon
summary: Roosevelt sits in on a session of the Argentine Congress, is received by Foreign Minister Bosch, and speaks at the Colon Theater to the Museo Social Argentino on "Democratic Ideals."

headline: Visiting schoolchildren
summary: Roosevelt visits schoolchildren in Buenos Aires. "Character and Civilization" is published in The Outlook.

events.detail: "Character and Civilization" appears in The Outlook

headline: Racetrack and farm show
summary: The party spends the day at the racecourse known as the Hippodrome and at the farm exposition.

events.detail: Visits the racecourse and the farm exposition

headline: An honorary degree and "Truths and Half Truths"
summary: The University of Buenos Aires gives Roosevelt an honorary doctor of laws, and he lectures at the Colon Theater on "Truths and Half Truths."

headline: A letter to Bamie
summary: From Buenos Aires, Roosevelt writes his sister Bamie about the journey.

headline: Troops at Campo de Mayo
summary: Roosevelt reviews troops at Campo de Mayo, stops at the Military Club, and speaks on "American Ideals" at a Museo Social Argentino banquet.

headline: Kermit is engaged
summary: A telegram reaches Kermit in Buenos Aires: Belle Willard has agreed to marry him.

events.detail: Kermit learns by telegram that Belle Willard accepts his proposal

headline: Edith feels left out
summary: Edith writes Ethel that she feels a little low, unable to help her husband and no longer needed by Kermit.

events.detail: Edith writes Ethel of feeling low

headline: Into the Argentine interior
summary: Roosevelt sets off into Santa Fe province, stopping at Rosario. "Democratic Ideals" appears in The Outlook, and he sends Sir Edward Grey a look back at the 1912 campaign.

events.detail: Leaves Buenos Aires for the interior

headline: Library and schools in Tucuman
summary: In Tucuman, Roosevelt visits the library and the industrial schools.

events.detail: Visits the library and industrial schools

headline: Sugar country
summary: Roosevelt tours sugar plantations around Tucuman.

headline: Three provincial capitals
summary: Traveling through Cordoba, San Luis and Mendoza, Roosevelt stops at the provincial capitals.

headline: Quentin turns 16
summary: Roosevelt is in Mendoza province. At Groton, Quentin turns 16.

headline: Wine country in Mendoza
summary: Roosevelt visits the agricultural college and wineries of Mendoza.

headline: Arriving in Chile
summary: Chilean officials welcome Roosevelt to Santiago.

headline: Lecture at the University of Chile
summary: Roosevelt calls on President Barros Luco and lectures to the University of Chile on democracy as a movement within a republic.

events.detail: University lecture on democracy as a movement within a republic

works.title: The Democratic Movement in a Republic

uncertain: The record names the president "Luce"; this is read as Ramon Barros Luco.

headline: In Santiago
summary: Roosevelt is in Santiago; nothing else is recorded.

headline: In Santiago
summary: Roosevelt is in Santiago; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Bamie's anniversary
summary: Roosevelt is in Santiago. At home, his sister Bamie marks 18 years of marriage.

headline: Edith sails for home
summary: At Valparaiso, Edith and Margaret leave Roosevelt and Kermit and board a ship for Panama. Roosevelt visits the Navy Club.

events.detail: Edith and Margaret depart by ship for Panama

headline: Valparaiso and Santiago
summary: Roosevelt sees the sights of Valparaiso, then attends a reception by the American community in Santiago.

headline: Chile's naval base
summary: Roosevelt tours the naval base at Talcahuano, then turns back toward Argentina.

headline: Across the Chilean lakes
summary: Setting out from Puerto Varas, Roosevelt and Kermit travel by boat over Lake Llanquihue and Lake Esmeralda to Peulla.
uncertain: The record misspells Peulla and calls Lago Todos los Santos "Lake Esmeralda."

headline: Over the Andes; the Autobiography appears
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit ride over the Andes to Lake Frias, then go by oxcart to Lake Nahuel Huapi and Bariloche. Back home, Scribner's publishes his Autobiography, and Boys' Life prints his "To All Boys."

events.detail: Ride across the Andes to Lake Frias
Oxcart to Lake Nahuel Huapi and Bariloche
"To All Boys" appears in Boys' Life

headline: Motoring across Patagonia
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit drive across the barren Patagonian plains.

headline: Anniversary in Neuquen
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit reach Neuquen. It is the 27th wedding anniversary of Roosevelt and Edith.

headline: Bahia Blanca naval base
summary: Heading back toward Buenos Aires, Roosevelt stops to see the naval base at Bahia Blanca.

headline: Horsemen and flowers
summary: Back in Buenos Aires, the city's equestrian society hosts Roosevelt at the Club Hipico, and he visits the flower festival.

headline: Bound for Paraguay
summary: Roosevelt leaves Buenos Aires for Asuncion.

headline: North through Entre Rios
summary: The journey north passes through the provinces of Entre Rios and Corrientes.

events.detail: Passes through Entre Rios and Corrientes

headline: Guests in Asuncion
summary: In Asuncion, Roosevelt and Kermit stay with a former president of Paraguay.

events.detail: Stay with a former Paraguayan president

headline: Villa Hayes with President Schaerer
summary: Roosevelt visits Villa Hayes with President Eduardo Schaerer.

events.detail: Visit to Villa Hayes with the president

headline: Up the Paraguay River
summary: In the afternoon Roosevelt starts up the Paraguay River aboard President Schaerer's yacht, with Tex Rickard along. His book Through the Brazilian Wilderness, and his 1913 diary, both pick up the story here.

events.detail: Leaves Asuncion upriver on the president's yacht

headline: Piranhas and a family letter
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit catch a piranha and reach Concepcion just before midnight. He writes Ted's wife Eleanor, glad she is expecting again, with news of Kermit, Archie and Quentin.

events.detail: Writes Eleanor about her coming baby and the boys

letters.topic: Delight at her new pregnancy; news of Kermit, Archie and Quentin

headline: Reviewing Paraguay's army
summary: In Concepcion, Roosevelt and Kermit stroll the streets, attend a reception, inspect army barracks, and Roosevelt speaks at City Hall. Back on the river he shoots two crocodilians. Edith and Margaret sail from Panama for home.

events.detail: Edith and Margaret sail from Panama toward home

tr_quotes.text: Left Concepcion about 9 a.m. Shot 2 crocs.

headline: Colonel Rondon comes aboard
summary: Steaming north through tropical country, the yacht reaches Brazil's border at the Apa River at noon, where Colonel Candido Rondon and the Brazilian members join. They take on wood at Porto Murtinho. Roosevelt writes Lodge that the Monroe Doctrine should rest on shared agreement.

events.detail: Steam upriver to the Brazilian border
Rondon and the Brazilian members join
Argues the Monroe Doctrine should be multilateral

letters.topic: Monroe Doctrine as a shared agreement among nations

headline: Six caymans
summary: Under gray skies, Father Zahm baptizes two children in a river town, and Roosevelt shoots caymans, which he likens to crocodiles.
uncertain: The record says six caymans; TR's diary says four.

headline: Under the flag past Coimbra
summary: Rain falls over marshy plains to the east as the boat, flying the American flag, passes Coimbra. Roosevelt later describes the river's golden sunsets in his book.

events.detail: Sunsets later described in Through the Brazilian Wilderness

headline: Reunion at Corumba
summary: At Corumba the town council hosts a reception and official dinner. Roosevelt and Kermit rejoin Cherrie and Miller, who have gathered about 800 bird and mammal specimens.

events.detail: Reception and dinner by the town council
Rejoin Cherrie and Miller, who have collected some 800 specimens

headline: Packing up at Corumba
summary: The expedition sorts and packs gear while Colonel Rondon checks supplies. Roosevelt hears plenty of animal tales, many about piranhas.

events.detail: Hears animal stories, including of piranhas

headline: Up the Taquari after an anteater
summary: Aboard the shallow river steamer Nyoac, the party heads up the Taquari toward Senhor de Barros's ranch, Las Palmeiras. Roosevelt shoots a giant anteater and many caymans, and they camp on shore.

events.detail: Up the Taquari toward the de Barros ranch
Shoots a giant anteater and many caymans

tr_quotes.text: Up the Taquary; shot many crocs; killed 1 tamandua, giant ant eater.

headline: Riding to the fazenda; Margaret ill
summary: The party rides 20 miles over five or six hours to the de Barros ranch, with baggage hauled by oxcart. In New York, Edith and Margaret arrive home, Margaret gravely ill.

events.detail: Ride to Las Palmeiras; baggage by oxcart
Margaret arrives in New York seriously ill

headline: Hunting the Pantanal
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit ride and hunt all day through the Pantanal swamp, and Kermit shoots a giant anteater.

events.detail: Day-long hunt on horseback in the swamp

tr_quotes.text: Hunted all day; Kermit killed another tamandud.

uncertain: Diary word 'tamandud' kept as given; read as tamandua.

headline: A jaguar for Roosevelt
summary: Kermit brings down two large marsh deer, and Roosevelt kills a jaguar and fires at a cayman.

events.detail: Roosevelt shoots a jaguar and takes a shot at a cayman

uncertain: Diary text partly crossed out in the original.

headline: Kermit's jaguar
summary: Kermit gets a jaguar and Roosevelt a capybara. They push their horses through a stream full of piranhas, and Roosevelt marvels at the birdlife.

events.detail: Kermit shoots a jaguar; TR a capybara

uncertain: Diary 'Shot jaguar 70 yards' may refer to Kermit's kill.

headline: Back toward the Taquari
summary: The party rides overland back to the Taquari. Roosevelt drops a wood ibis in flight.

events.detail: Shoots a wood ibis on the wing

headline: Downriver; the Federal Reserve becomes law
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit ride to the boat and steam downstream, towing a small craft for a peon. In Washington, the Federal Reserve Act is signed into law.

events.detail: Ride to the boat, then steam down the Taquari

headline: The River of Doubt party assembles
summary: Back at Corumba, Roosevelt and Kermit rejoin the rest aboard the Nyoac. The party includes Harper, Father Zahm and his aide Jacob Sigg, Cherrie, Miller, Fiala, Colonel Rondon, Captain Magalhaes, Lieutenants Lyra and Filho, geologist Oliveira and taxidermist Reinisch. Roosevelt writes Edith.

events.detail: Return to Corumba and rejoin the expedition on the Nyoac

headline: Christmas on the Paraguay
summary: On Christmas the Nyoac pushes upstream against a strong current, the expedition on deck and Kermit busy preparing skins.

headline: Flies and heat on the Sao Lourenco
summary: The Nyoac turns up the narrower Sao Lourenco, with biting flies everywhere and the thermometer at 100 degrees.

headline: Rain on the Cuiaba
summary: Steaming up the Cuiaba in heavy rain, the boat pulls in at a ranch to take on milk and beef.

events.detail: Ranch stop to take on milk and beef

headline: Welcome at Sao Joao
summary: The party reaches Sao Joao, the ranch of Brazil's agriculture secretary, Senhor da Costa Marques, for a big reception. Afternoon rain, 97 degrees.

events.detail: Reach Sao Joao Fazenda; large reception

headline: A peccary with a spear
summary: Father and son da Costa Marques take the party out after jaguars on an overcast day. Roosevelt kills a wild boar with a spear before heavy rain sets in.

events.detail: Jaguar hunt with the da Costa Marques men

headline: Downstream in a downpour
summary: In soaking rain the party heads back down the Cuiaba to the Sao Lourenco and anchors by the bank for the night.

events.detail: Descend the Cuiaba into the Sao Lourenco; anchor for the night

headline: Machetes, ants and a capybara
summary: In steady rain the hunters cut through dense jungle, beset by mosquitoes and fire ants. Roosevelt shoots a monkey, the party bags coatis and bush deer, and when the sun breaks through around 2 he gets a capybara. Packed for the trip: Gibbon, Sophocles, More's Utopia, Marcus Aurelius and Epictetus.

events.detail: Hunt on foot through jungle, cutting a path with machetes
Shoots a monkey; party takes coatis and bush deer
Shoots a capybara after the rain stops
His expedition books include Gibbon, Sophocles, Utopia, Marcus Aurelius and Epictetus

uncertain: The record adds "[tapir]" after capybara, which is unclear. TR's 1913 diary ends here.

headline: A hard, empty New Year's hunt
summary: Up at 5, the party eats hardtack, ham, sardines and coffee, then tramps all day through jungle and marsh in the heat and comes back with nothing.

events.detail: All-day hunt on foot through jungle and marsh; no game

headline: Back onto the Paraguay
summary: The expedition runs down the Sao Lourenco to the Paraguay and begins working upstream.

events.detail: Down the Sao Lourenco, then up the Paraguay

headline: Parakeets on the river; Margaret dies
summary: Steaming up the Paraguay, Roosevelt watches parakeets build nests. At home, Margaret Roosevelt, who sailed south with the party, dies of typhoid fever.

headline: Quiet nights on deck
summary: Going up the Paraguay, the party watches wildlife by day and enjoys calm nights on deck.

headline: At Sao Luis de Caceres
summary: Leaving the marshes behind, the party reaches Sao Luis de Caceres late in the day, and Roosevelt stays with Lieutenant Lyra. In the United States, Margaret Roosevelt is buried.

events.detail: Reach Sao Luis de Caceres; stays at Lieutenant Lyra's house

headline: Up the River of Tapirs
summary: The expedition heads up the Sepotuba, known as the River of Tapirs, and pitches camp at Porto Campo. Baggage goes ahead to a staging point, and the flag is raised each day.

events.detail: Up the Sepotuba to Porto Campo; camp made

headline: Camp life at Porto Campo
summary: At Porto Campo the party observes wildlife and hunts.

headline: In camp
summary: The expedition stays in camp at Porto Campo.

headline: A tapir in the water
summary: With four canoes, three dugouts and one Canadian, the party hunts tapir. Hunting on foot with Fiala, Roosevelt takes a bush deer and later shoots a tapir as it swims.

events.detail: Tapir hunt by canoe; TR on foot with Fiala gets a bush deer and a tapir

headline: Peccaries elude them
summary: A hunt for white-lipped peccaries comes up empty, and the bugs make it miserable: ticks, wasps, mosquitoes and fire ants.

headline: Five peccaries with Rondon
summary: Roosevelt and Colonel Rondon try again for peccaries and get five, plus a small bush deer.

events.detail: Kill five peccaries and a bush deer

headline: The supply boat is back
summary: The supply boat comes back to camp at Porto Campo.

headline: Breaking camp for Tapirapoan
summary: The party strikes camp, packs a launch and houseboat, and starts up the Paraguay for Tapirapoan with 30 men and five dogs, in rain.

events.detail: Break camp and load the boats; 30 men, five dogs

headline: Reading Gibbon at a mile and a half an hour
summary: The boat crawls upriver while the men cook on deck over a makeshift hearth. Roosevelt's reading includes Gibbon, Scott's Quentin Durward and the Song of Roland. At home, Alice's grandmother Lee dies, leaving her an annual income from a trust.

events.detail: Reads Gibbon, Scott's Quentin Durward and the Song of Roland

headline: Ants in the tents
summary: A man who went missing is found, lunch is on an island, and the party reaches Tapirapoan. Ants chew through their tents at night.

events.detail: Lost man recovered; lunch on an island

headline: Into the real wilderness
summary: At Tapirapoan, Roosevelt readies for the unexplored country with Kermit, Colonel Rondon, Cherrie, Miller, Fiala, two Brazilians and the paddlers. He writes Quentin about the trip and Kermit, and reports early results to Frank Chapman.

events.detail: Expedition assembles for the overland stage
Writes Quentin about the trip and Kermit
Reports results so far to Chapman

letters.topic: The trip so far; news of Kermit

tr_quotes.text: We are now about to go into the real wilderness . . . In a month or 6 weeks we shall reach the headwaters of an unexplored river.

uncertain: The record does not say which letter holds the quotation.

headline: Vampire bats
summary: At Tapirapoan, Roosevelt studies vampire bats.

headline: The ox train goes ahead
summary: Seventy pack oxen leave Tapirapoan ahead of the party. In the United States, Bamie turns 59.

headline: Kermit hunts
summary: At Tapirapoan, Kermit goes out hunting.

headline: At Tapirapoan
summary: The expedition is at Tapirapoan; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Mule train to the Sepotuba falls
summary: The party sets out on riding mules and covers 15 miles to the Sepotuba waterfall.

headline: Hacking through the forest
summary: Turning west away from the river, the riders cut their way through dense forest with machetes and make camp in rain.

events.detail: West through thick forest, clearing with machetes

headline: Up onto the Parecis Plateau
summary: A steep climb brings the party to the rim of the Parecis Plateau, where the day is cool and free of mosquitoes.

headline: Over the great divide
summary: Riding across the high plateau, the party passes the watershed that separates the Amazon basin from the Paraguay's, with rain in the afternoon.

events.detail: Cross the plateau and the Paraguay-Amazon divide

headline: Campfire stories
summary: Heading north, Kermit shoots two pampas deer bucks. That night stories go around the campfire while Roosevelt writes; it rains.

events.detail: Writes in camp while others tell stories

headline: On the trail
summary: The expedition is traveling; nothing else is recorded.

headline: On the trail
summary: The expedition is traveling; nothing else is recorded.

headline: Riding in heavy rain
summary: The expedition travels on through heavy rain.

headline: Telegraph line and a swim
summary: After a late start the party strikes a telegraph line, crosses the Sacre, and sees the falls at Salto Bello, where the motor road ends. The men go swimming.

events.detail: Reach the telegraph line and cross the Sacre
See the waterfall at Salto Bello

headline: A ball game near Utiarity
summary: Two miles from Utiarity Falls, Roosevelt watches Indians play an unusual form of ball. It rains.

events.detail: Watches Indigenous players' distinctive ball game

headline: Rain at Utiarity Falls
summary: The expedition is at Utiarity Falls in the rain.
